ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure there are two congruent isosceles right triangles, with the legs respectively being the vertical side and the horizontal side, and the hypotenuse slanting downward to the right. The square P inside the left triangle is parallel to the two legs, is located at the right-angle vertex, and its upper right corner touches the hypotenuse. The square R inside the right triangle is a square rotated into a rhombus shape; its left vertex touches the vertical side, its bottom vertex touches the horizontal side, and the other two vertices touch the hypotenuse. Reasoning: Suppose the leg lengths of the two congruent isosceles right triangles are both L. Take the right-angle vertex as the origin and the horizontal and vertical legs as the coordinate axes; then the equation of the hypotenuse can be written as x+y=L. For square P, let its side length be p. The coordinates of its upper right corner are (p,p), and it is on the hypotenuse, so p+p=L, that is, L=2p. It is known that the area of P is 45, therefore p^2=45, so L^2=(2p)^2=4p^2=180. For square R, suppose the horizontal or vertical distance from its center to the left, right, upper, and lower vertices is d; then its horizontal and vertical diagonal lengths are both 2d. From the contact relationships in the figure, one can let the left vertex be (0,d), the bottom vertex be (d,0), and the center be (d,d); then the upper vertex is (d,2d), and the right vertex is (2d,d). The upper vertex and the right vertex are both on the hypotenuse x+y=L, therefore L=3d. The diagonal length of square R is 2d, so its area is (2d)^2/2=2d^2. From d=L/3, the area of R is 2L^2/9=2×180/9=40.

What is the area, in $\mathrm{cm}^{2}$, of the square $\mathrm{R}$ ? <image1>

method.method_draft: Use a coordinate-length model. From the image, read that each large triangle is a 45-45-90 right triangle with perpendicular legs vertical and horizontal and hypotenuse slanting down; square P is axis-aligned in the right-angle corner with its upper-right vertex on the hypotenuse, while square R is a tilted diamond whose left and bottom vertices touch the two legs and whose top and right vertices touch the hypotenuse. From the text, use that the two triangles are congruent and area(P)=45. Let the common leg length be L. For P, if its side is p, the hypotenuse condition in an isosceles right triangle gives p+p=L, so p=L/2 and p^2=45, hence L^2=180. For R, let d be the half-diagonal distance from its center to a vertex in the horizontal/vertical directions; then its left and bottom vertices are d from the right-angle corner, and its top/right vertices are at coordinates adding to 3d, so the hypotenuse condition gives L=3d. The area of R is the area of a square with diagonal 2d, namely (2d)^2/2=2d^2=2L^2/9=40.
method.CoT_raw:
图像描述：图中有两个全等的等腰直角三角形，直角边分别是竖直边和水平边，斜边向右下方倾斜。左边三角形内的正方形 P 与两条直角边平行，位于直角顶点处，其右上角接触斜边。右边三角形内的正方形 R 是旋转成菱形状的正方形，其左顶点接触竖直边，底顶点接触水平边，另外两个顶点接触斜边。

推理：设两个全等等腰直角三角形的直角边长都是 L。取直角顶点为原点，水平、竖直直角边为坐标轴，则斜边方程可写为 x+y=L。

对于正方形 P，设边长为 p。它的右上角坐标为 (p,p)，且在斜边上，所以 p+p=L，即 L=2p。已知 P 的面积为 45，因此 p^2=45，所以 L^2=(2p)^2=4p^2=180。

对于正方形 R，设它从中心到左、右、上、下顶点的水平或竖直距离为 d，则其水平、竖直对角线长均为 2d。由图中接触关系，可令左顶点为 (0,d)，底顶点为 (d,0)，中心为 (d,d)，则上顶点为 (d,2d)，右顶点为 (2d,d)。上顶点和右顶点都在斜边 x+y=L 上，因此 L=3d。

正方形 R 的对角线长为 2d，所以面积为 (2d)^2/2=2d^2。由 d=L/3，得 R 的面积为 2L^2/9=2×180/9=40。

method.method_draft: Use area fractions instead of first finding the side of R. From the image, read the same two configurations: P is the standard square fitted into the right-angle corner of a 45-45-90 triangle, and R is the diamond square whose vertices touch the two legs and the hypotenuse as shown. From the text, use that both enclosing triangles are congruent and area(P)=45. In the P configuration, the square side is half the leg of the isosceles right triangle, so P occupies one-half of the whole triangle’s area; therefore the area of each large triangle is 90. For R, compare it to its enclosing triangle by letting the small right-angle-corner triangle cut off by R have equal legs 1. Then the large triangle leg is 3 in the same units, while R has diagonals 2 and 2, so area(R)=2 in these units and area(large triangle)=9/2. Thus R is a fraction 2/(9/2)=4/9 of the large triangle. Therefore area(R)=(4/9)·90=40.
method.CoT_raw:
Image description: The figure shows two congruent isosceles right triangles, each with the right angle at the lower-left corner. In the left triangle, square P is placed in the right-angle corner with its sides parallel to the triangle legs, and its opposite corner touches the hypotenuse. In the right triangle, square R is tilted like a diamond: it touches the two legs near the lower-left corner and also touches the hypotenuse as shown.
Reasoning: Since the two enclosing triangles are congruent, they have the same area. For square P, if the leg length of the isosceles right triangle is L, the square side is L/2 because its opposite corner lies on the 45-degree hypotenuse. Thus area(P) = L^2/4, while the triangle area is L^2/2, so P is half the triangle. Given area(P) = 45, each large triangle has area 90. For square R, use the proportional setup from the diagram: let the small right-angle-corner triangle cut off by R have equal legs 1. Then the large triangle leg is 3, and R has perpendicular diagonals of lengths 2 and 2, so area(R) = (2·2)/2 = 2 in these units. The large triangle area is 3·3/2 = 9/2, so R occupies 2/(9/2) = 4/9 of its enclosing triangle. Therefore area(R) = (4/9)·90 = 40.
